[[File:Obi-Wan_hyperdrive_ring.png|thumb|right|250px|A [[Syliure-31 hyperspace docking ring/Legends|Syluire-31 hyperspace docking ring]] with a [[Delta-7B Aethersprite-class light interceptor/Legends|Delta-7B ''Aethersprite''-class light interceptor]]]]
The '''hyperspace transport ring''', also known as a '''hyperdrive ring''', '''hyperdrive booster ring''', or '''hyperspace docking ring''', was a device used to achieve faster-than-light travel by [[Starship/Legends|starships]] with no onboard [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]].

==Characteristics==
[[File:Eta2_hyperring.png|thumb|left|200px|A [[Syliure-45 hyperdrive module/Legends|Syliure-45 hyperdrive module]] for an [[Eta-2 Actis-class interceptor/Legends|Eta-2 ''Actis''-class Jedi Starfighter]]]]
During the millennia of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], many [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] were too small to safely contain a hyperdrive, so in order to travel through [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] these ships were required to connect to a Hyperdrive Ring. These rings were usually powered by twin reactors and [[Ion engine/Legends|ion drives]]; the ring contained [[Hypermatter/Legends|hypermatter]], providing ballast for the attached starfighter during the jump to hyperspace. Variant models could be equipped with additional acceleration pods, increasing both their sublight and supralight speed. In all cases, once a hyperspace jump was complete, the starfighter disengaged from the booster ring, which remained anchored in space, awaiting the ship's return.

This was seen as a vulnerability by some, for if the booster ring was destroyed, the starfighter would be stranded. Starfighters used by the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] were equipped with adaptable long-range communication relays, which allowed the pilot to contact the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] for assistance in these instances. Some Jedi, like [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], modified their ships to contain ultra miniaturized-hyperdrives, eliminating the vulnerability, at a cost to the hyperdrive's performance and range.

==History==
[[File:V-19_hyperdrive_ring.png|thumb|right|A [[V-19 Torrent starfighter/Legends|V-19 Torrent starfighter]] hyperdrive ring]]

The [[Delta-7 Aethersprite-class light interceptor/Legends|Delta-7 ''Aethersprite''-class light interceptor]], [[Delta-7B Aethersprite-class light interceptor/Legends|Delta-7B ''Aethersprite''-class light interceptor]], and the Eta-2 ''Actis''-class light interceptor were three of the most visible users of the Hyperdrive Ring Technology. [[Rho-1 Limulus-class courier/Legends|Rho-1 ''Limulus''-class couriers]] also used them, and the [[Koros Spaceworks interceptor]]s had rings modified for their benefit.

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the two most popular variations of hyperdrive rings were the [[Syliure-31 hyperspace docking ring/Legends|Syliure-31 long-range hyperdrive module]] and the [[Syliure-45 hyperdrive module/Legends|Syliure-45 hyperdrive module]]. Both were manufactured by [[TransGalMeg Industries, Incorporated|TransGalMeg Industries]], thanks in part to a lucrative subcontract they received from [[Kuat Drive Yards/Legends|Kuat Drive Yards]], builders of the starfighters of the Jedi Order.
